introduction: Nebraska Child Care Subsidy starts with iServe and a telephone interview. Parents must also use a DHHS-approved provider before program payments can begin.
description: Nebraska Child Care Subsidy starts with iServe and a telephone interview. Parents must also use a DHHS-approved provider before program payments can begin.

sections.who: Qualifying parental activities include work, Employment First, school or training, specified medical visits or a medically confirmed illness or injury. In a two-parent household, both parents must meet an eligible activity concurrently. Children generally are 12 or younger, with specified authorization and special-needs exceptions.
sections.get: The subsidy helps pay childcare costs. Depending on income, a family may owe a fee to the provider; DHHS pays the approved remainder.
sections.docs:
• Prepare earned and unearned household income records.
  • Have the child’s age, care needs and provider information available.
  • Keep work, school or medical information relevant to the requested care.
sections.apply:
1. Apply through iServe

    Use iServe Nebraska and complete the telephone interview.

  2. Check provider approval

    Ask whether the provider is DHHS-approved. A friend or relative may need a provider referral and approval process.

  3. Confirm authorization

    Read the decision for approved care and any family fee before assuming payments cover an arrangement.
sections.after: Report changes in care needs or provider through DHHS. Do not assume a provider-referral date guarantees backdated payment.
sections.sources: Checked October 1, 2026 using Nebraska parent eligibility and provider guidance. USA Assistance background guide. Program staff determine eligibility and available assistance.

faqs: Can a special-needs teenager receive care?
The parent guidance describes assistance up to age 19 when care is required because of a special need.
Can I use a family member as provider?
Possibly, but the person must complete DHHS’s approval process.
Can care start being paid while approval is pending?
DHHS says payment begins after provider approval and is not backdated to the referral date.

provenance.scope: Published eligibility, service purpose and application pathway; no unverified financial limits or deadlines included.
